cards.explanation: The answer is that allowed isn't always helpful, friends. Paul says, “Everything is permissible…” but not everything is beneficial. So "allowed" and "helpful" are two different questions, and he wants them both asked. I'm allowed to eat a whole tray of warm cookies, but my apron strings would file a complaint.

Paul tells them to seek the good of others, friends. He says, “No one should seek his own good, but the good of others.” (1 Corinthians 10:24) He points everyone's eyes away from their own plate and toward the person next to them. In my bakery, that means the first cookie goes in somebody else's box, not my apron pocket.

The answer is to eat it without raising questions, bakers. Paul says, “Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions of conscience…” (1 Corinthians 10:25) So no worrying over every package. He gives his reason in the very next verse.

The word is Lord, friends. Paul quotes it: “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.” (1 Corinthians 10:26) It comes from Psalm 24:1. Everything in that market sits inside what belongs to Him. That's the reason Paul gives.

The answer is True, bakers. Paul says, “If an unbeliever invites you to a meal and you want to go, eat anything set before you without raising questions of conscience.” (1 Corinthians 10:27) Notice that the believer in this scene wants to go. Once you're there, you can eat without quizzing the host.

Paul says don't eat it, friends. Once someone tells you the food was offered to idols, he says, “then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for the sake of conscience…” (1 Corinthians 10:28) The moment someone says that out loud, the answer changes. The two reasons he gives are the person who spoke up and conscience.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says to skip it for the sake of “…the other one’s conscience, I mean, not your own.” (1 Corinthians 10:29) Right there in the verse he says whose it is: the other one's, not yours. The conscience at stake belongs to the person who said something.

The answer is God, bakers. Paul says, “So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all to the glory of God.” (1 Corinthians 10:31) Eating, drinking and everything else all land under that one line. Nothing in your day falls outside it.

The answer is False, friends. Paul says, “Do not become a stumbling block, whether to Jews or Greeks or the church of God…” (1 Corinthians 10:32) He names three groups, and the church is just one of them. Jews and Greeks are in there too, so it isn't only about fellow believers.

The word is saved, bakers. Paul says, “…I am not seeking my own good, but the good of many, that they may be saved.” (1 Corinthians 10:33) That's the goal he states. He's after the good of many, not his own.

The answer is Christ, friends. Paul says, “You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.” (1 Corinthians 11:1) So he points past himself to the One he's following. I'm glad that's how it goes, because my mustache is not a safe thing to imitate.
